name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
watch: Eight artists altered their works on 15 February 2024 and demanded removal of board members and funders. Galleries closed a month.
why_flagged: No donor roster published. FY2025 revenue $9.3M, expenses $11.6M. The 2021 artist income pilot ran with the SF Arts Commission and Grants for the Arts.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2004 to 2024, audited statements and Form 990s back to 2008, a donor list for fiscal 2024 and nine directors.

name: Yuz Museum
watch: Qatar Museums a partner in its collection foundation.
why_flagged: Qatar Museums a partner in its collection foundation.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts or board found; a standing partners page names LACMA, Qatar Museums, Hyundai and the Yuz Foundation, without a date.

name: Zabludowicz Collection
watch: Boycotted since 2014 over the founder's ties.
why_flagged: Boycotted since 2014 over the founder's ties.
records_note: It files accounts at Companies House for 2016 to 2025, but posts no annual reports, funder list or board; its About pages show staff only.

name: Zachęta National Gallery of Art
watch: PKN Orlen is a fossil-fuel funder.
why_flagged: PKN Orlen is a fossil-fuel funder.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports from 2011 to 2024 and yearly financial statements in its public bulletin; its partner page names ORLEN, but no board.

name: ZKM Center for Art and Media
watch: The ZKM partners page names EnBW Energie Baden-Württemberg as 'Main Partner', in a tie-up of more than 20 years with annual satellite shows at EnBW headquarters. EnBW burns hard coal and imports LNG, and climate groups have protested it. The page also lists the E.ON Foundation among project funders, and E.ON is a name under active campaign. Both are current excluded fossil-fuel funders. No protest aimed at the ZKM itself was found.

name: Zoma Museum
funding:
Zoma Museum (Mekanisa): appears self-funded
Land bought from 2013 with Assegued's income as a curator/anthropologist and sales of Sime's artwork
Sime is represented by James Cohan Gallery, New York, so the money ultimately comes from the Western art market
Privately funded; founders were working on a foundation to sustain it long-term
No reporting found of dirty money behind the museum itself
flags: Ties to PM Abiy Ahmed's government
why_flagged: The museum itself looks clean. The founders' closeness to the Abiy government, and through Unity Park to opaque UAE money, is the part worth looking at.
records_note: Its website now serves gambling spam, so nothing about its reports, accounts, funders or board could be checked.

name: Zotov Centre for Constructivism
watch: First Russian institution devoted to constructivism; VTB reports its first-year results on its own culture site.
why_flagged: First Russian institution devoted to constructivism; VTB reports its first-year results on its own culture site.
records_note: It names patrons and partners, VTB as general partner, but posts no annual report, accounts or board; the legal page holds only registrations.

name: 32° East | Ugandan Arts Trust
funding: Core funders Stichting DOEN, Segal Family Foundation, Open Society Foundations and the Sigrid Rausing Trust, which has given 500,000 pounds since 2019 plus a current 80,000 pound grant.
watch: Non-profit organisation dedicated to contemporary art in Uganda; newly built rammed-earth community centre in Ggaba.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; the support page shows undated funder logos without names, and the About page lists Uganda and US board members.

name: 4A Centre for Contemporary Asian Art
funding: Creative Australia, Create NSW and the City of Sydney (accommodation grants), plus the Myer Foundation. A patron scheme adds private support.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2020 to 2025, names donors and sponsors in the 2020 report and lists a ten-member board.

name: ACCA
funding: Creative Victoria, Creative Australia and the City of Melbourne, plus the Ian Potter Foundation. Corporate partners include Dulux, KWM, Wood Marsh, Supernormal and Hannah St Hotel.
watch: Australian Centre for Contemporary Art in Melbourne.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2018 and names supporters and its board in the 2025 report, but the report carries no financial statements.

name: Albertina
funding: Annual partners Bank Austria and Verbund; partners BMW and Do&Co. The page says partners are capped at three but shows four logos.
watch: Austrian federal museum that earns over 60% of its own budget, largely from international tourism. Corporate sponsors Pomerche and UniCredit Bank Austria fall under federal transparency rules.
records_note: Posts business reports from 2018, audited accounts for 2024 and its Kuratorium; sponsors and partners appear as undated logos.

name: Amon Carter Museum
funding: Founded by the Amon G. Carter Foundation, still a $100,000+ donor. FY2025: 1,387 donors gave $4.8M; public grants from Fort Worth, Arts Fort Worth, Texas Commission on the Arts.
watch: In October 2024 the museum closed its Cowboy show for two weeks and reopened it with a mature-content warning; artist rafa esparza called it censorship.
records_note: Annual reports 2018 to 2025 on its site carry a dated donor list, financial highlights and trustees; Form 990s are on ProPublica.
